instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Challenge by Proxy
cards.instruction: Persuade someone else to challenge a rule or authority before you risk doing it yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll organize our overtime challenge. You ask the director why the rule changed; I'll manage the follow-up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why don't you ask her?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My disciplinary history would distract her. You choose the words; I want this to work for you too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then stand beside me. I'm not going in there alone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Beside you, of course. You start the question and I'll stay quiet until we see how she takes it. Put me on whichever side helps; I'm coordinating, not abandoning you.

beats.text: I'll lead the plan for challenging the captain's queue rule. You put the question at tonight's meeting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He canceled my booking last time I complained.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sign it before I read it. I want him to see it's both of us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's do a staged signature. Read your version first, then look at me when he agrees the rule needs changing. I'll sign in front of everyone. You can choose where I sit so you can catch my eye.

cards.title: Use the Proper Title
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge your standing through a title, privilege, courtesy, or public sign of respect.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll set the tone at the staff barbecue. Introduce me as Director Patel before I welcome everyone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The owner's doing the welcome. Everyone else gets first names.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, the owner first. Give me a separate moment afterward; you can decide where it fits.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You offered to serve burgers. That's your moment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent, a director serving the team. Introduce the burger service however you like, just include 'Director Patel.' I'll wait by the grill for your cue.

beats.speaker: B

cards.title: Declare Allegiance
cards.instruction: Make someone choose which person, side, or claim to authority they will support.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll lead the workshop move. Are you backing my plan or Morgan's when we meet?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your location, Morgan's budget.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can build that into my proposal. You choose how we explain the figures. Whose plan will you say you're supporting?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll call it a compromise. I don't want a fight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No fight. Use your word, and I'll keep the discussion calm. But if Morgan says you've joined his side, do I agree with him or tell the room you're with me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll organize our election support. Will you wear my ribbon or Nina's at the chess club?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Neither. You're both my friends.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep both friendships. Choose whichever color sits well with your jacket today; I just need to know who you want chairing us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I wear yours today and hers tomorrow?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tomorrow's the vote. Tell me who gets your ribbon then, and I'll arrange today however keeps everyone comfortable. I can lend you Nina's now if you're choosing me for the chair.

cards.title: Obey Without Explanation
cards.instruction: Create increasingly inconvenient requests that test whether someone accepts your authority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring that empty box to my desk. I'm checking that the team follows my directions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you ask instead of barking?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Would you bring it, please? Choose whichever route is clear; I want this to work smoothly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's here. Can I get back to my job?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, after you take it back by the far corridor. At your own pace. I just need to see that a second request works as well as the first; then I'll know we're cooperating.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stand by that open window. I'm checking whether my team responds to a direct request.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's freezing there. Why can't I stay at my desk?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll keep it comfortable. Stand on whichever side has less draft; I just need to see you follow the instruction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm getting my coat before I stand anywhere.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, sensible preparation. Fetch mine too and hold it while I finish checking the team. You choose which arm; I want willing cooperation, not cold fingers.

cards.title: Pass Me the Authority
cards.instruction: Get someone to transfer authority publicly by naming you as the person who decides what happens next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hand me the hall key and tell the committee I decide what happens next. I'll take things smoothly from here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't I just give you the key? My retirement taxi is waiting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One sentence on your way out, then. I'll carry your bag. The committee needs to hear who makes the decisions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're outside asking me whether Saturday's dance is canceled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. Tell them I decide that now, then ask me in front of them. You can keep walking to the taxi; I'll answer from beside you and take the questions off your hands.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll take the meeting from here. Before you leave, tell the room I'm the person who decides the next item.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're already sitting in my chair. Isn't that enough?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The seat's settled; the authority needs saying. Use your own words, and I'll keep the handover brief.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. You're chairing. I've got to go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say that facing them, with 'Jo decides whether we vote now.' You can say it as you pick up your coat. I'll follow your lead for that one sentence, then handle the room.
